title: PRESSER | Chris Beard & Budd Clark - Arizona Postgame (11-25-26)
text: All right, please welcome Miss NS to the uh media room. We have head coach Chris Beard and Bud Clark joining us this morning. Coach, um you go two and one in Maui. What did you see from your team this entire week? >> Yeah, I think first of all overall it's a great experience for our team to come to the Maui Invitational for the first time. Old Miss's first trip and so we came here to win three games and gave ourselves a chance today. Um but just go home with two wins. But um this tournament has the reputation it has for a reason and uh just better than advertised from the hospitality at the hotel, the gym, the people here on the island. Uh just a big thank you from everybody in our organization. I think the basketball game today uh tip your hat to the opponent. There's a reason Arizona is a final four contender, a top 10 current team. Um I think you got to give our guys a lot of credit, too. I think in the first half we controlled the game. In the second half, uh Arizona controlled the game. and we just need a little we need a couple more four-minute games in that second half go our way and we just didn't get it done. Give them credit. Um you know their post player uh is a problem. Give him a lot of credit. Um we had some plans and the plans just didn't work out today. But I thought our team got better today through competition. I don't think you judge it just based on the 40minute result. I think there's a lot of segments in the game where we imposed our identity. Uh and certainly we got some valuable film to watch when we get back to Oxford. you know, playing against one of the best teams in the country gives us a chance to get better. I thought our guys competed this weekend. Um, just like Arizona, I I think we are one of the better teams in the country in my opinion. >> Any questions for uh Bud? >> Yeah. Um, Bud over here, you had five steals against BYU. With Arizona's defense and size, what made you either stay home or attack those passing lanes? Um, I feel like I still was in attack mode regardless of who they were. Um, I just feel like they executed a little bit better. >> Uh, but over here points in the paint. You guys had 32. Uh, obviously with Crievis in there, it's more difficult to get to the rim. Uh, was that a challenge more in the second half than the first? >> Uh, yeah. You see the guy 73. So, it's definitely a challenge when you got a 7-3 dude just sitting in the paint the whole game. And uh what do you take out of this experience these three games? >> Um I feel like we can play with anybody in the country no matter who they are. Like coach who said I just feel like we one of the better teams in the country and I feel like we proved a lot this tournament. But uh moving forward um after this um how do you see your role still evolving as the the number one on the team running the game managing um as your team continues to get better? >> Um I just want to win. Whatever coach needs me to do, I'll do. Uh so whether it's scoring, passing, playing defense, I'm just doing whatever it takes to win. >> All right, Bob, let you head out with your team. Any questions for coach? Chris, how do you deal with a big guy like Crievis? Obviously, you don't have one that size, but you did a good job in the first half. Was that just keeping him off balance and out of, you know, defending the rim? >> Yeah, I think in the first half we were having some success on defending the feeders. Um, I think Tommy made some adjustments, got that ball in the middle of the floor that put a lot of pressure on us. U, we needed some more deflections on the passer today. Okay, we had a couple timely mistakes. Um, no, he's a load. And I think when you play Arizona, you got to decide, you take away the threes, um, and deal with like a 30-point game that we dealt with today, and we didn't do either. They hit some timely threes. So, I think this stat sheet would have been okay if Arizona would hit two or three threes. So, the combination of their timely three-point shooting, um, the best big on the floor today. Um, you know, the game's got to be called a certain way, too. I think, you know, he he played 35 minutes and he only had one foul. Um, and he fouls out two or three of our guys. So, we're a no excuse program. Uh, but I am interested in getting to the laptop quickly just to see, you know, what we can do a better job um of not fouling. And he's obviously doing a great job, you know, convincing the officials he's not fouling. But 35 minutes, you guys saw it. For him to have one foul, that's a little puzzling to me. Um, coach, were there any growth in some of the players that you saw today that you didn't see in the preseason? >> Yeah, absolutely. That's one of the benefits of these Thanksgiving time tournaments, you know, to play three straight powerful opponents. Uh, you learn a lot about your team. Um, every team is tested. Arizona as well tipped their hat. They had three games in three days. Um, and so, yeah, for sure. I think, um, obviously our objective was to try to win three games. We got two wins, but equally important, you know, our team's a work in progress. Uh, three returners, three freshman, nine new players. I think we did a lot of good things, including today. You know, I mean, maybe the best we played in this tournament in our 120 minutes was, you know, a lot of the minutes against Arizona today. Uh, you know, by far the best team we played in this tournament was Arizona. >> Anything else for coach? >> Coach, how proud of you are um of you as a team? um forcing Clemson and BYU with such big turnovers. Your defense has just been incredible this tournament. >> Yeah, I think every team in college basketball has a defensive identity. You know, some people are going to do it with size, length, athleticism. They're their different ways to play defense and basketball, but um not just this year. Our teams have always valued trying to uh be hard to score against and and try to turn the opponents over. And um today we had some success. I know we forced more turnovers than we turned it over, but we needed a few more to be successful in kind of a heavyweight battle like this. Um, but no, I think that's a big part of our defense. We try to explain to our guys, defense isn't, you know, hoping a guy misses when he gets the ball. Uh, defense is getting the ball, you know, not even giving him a shot. I think we did a really good job for the most part in our three games this week in Maui doing that. We just needed we needed a little bit more help down the stretch. Give Arizona credit. um they really just kind of turned into a really deliberate high low situation and um didn't give us any chances really to turn them over in that set whether except if we were a bit more busy on the ball, get some deflections, but I thought their feeders did a really well job. I think big fella will get all the credit. He probably just got the trophy, but somebody was throwing him the ball and I was really impressed uh with the Arizona feeders uh that were giving him the ball. All >> right. Thanks, coach. Thank you.
